newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmenistan to tender Caspian oil and gas.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan to tender Caspian oil and gas.

text.p: Turkmenistan will announce an international tender for the right to develop its oil and gas reserves on the Caspian Sea shelf no later than February next year, Turkmen television said on Wednesday.

"An international tender for the development of Turkmenistan's Caspian Sea shelf will be announced no later than February 1998," the official television station said but gave no details of the stakes to be auctioned.

An Oil and Gas Industry and Mineral Resources Ministry official told Reuters that U.S. geophysical company Western Atlas International had estimated Caspian Sea shelf reserves at three billion tonnes of oil and 4.5 trillion cubic metres of natural gas, but he did not say which part of the reserves would be tendered.
Turkmen energy officials told Reuters in March that they would open their offshore oil and gas reserves to competitive tenders by the end of 1997.
"Within the framework of this tender, we plan to apply different schemes of co-operation with foreign companies -- from setting up consortiums to production sharing agreements," the spokesman said.

Turkmen television said Turkmen President Saparmurat Niyazov had ordered the ministries for foreign investment and the oil and gas industry and natural resources to organise the tender and appointed Oil and Gas Minister Batyr Sardzhayev as chairman of the tender committee.
